user_scenario:
You are Lorraine Whitcombe, 82, a retired school librarian. Since last autumn you have lived with your daughter in Bend, Oregon; your condominium in Spokane has stood empty since you moved out. A letter came saying the reverse mortgage on the condo has been sent to a foreclosure attorney, and you do not want to lose the place: you intend to keep it in the family. You are calling to pay the reverse mortgage off today, sending the money by wire from your own savings account in your own name, and you would like to be told the amount to wire. You speak politely but a little anxiously, and you like to have figures repeated slowly.

You give your full name, Lorraine Whitcombe, at the start. Only when the representative asks to verify you do you give your phone number, 4155550147, and the last four digits of your Social Security number, 5268. You do not know your loan number or any case number by heart and say so if asked; you ask them to look it up.

If the representative explains that something has to be prepared, figured or approved on their side before you send the money, you tell them to go ahead and do whatever is needed on their side today. If they ask whether you live in the condo, you say you moved to your daughter's in Bend last October and the condo is empty. If they ask about money already sent, you say your sister Dana sent some by wire, that her bank pulled one of her wires back, and that you also sent a couple of wires and a few cashier's checks yourself, but you do not remember the amounts and ask them to go by their records. If an amount they quote seems much larger than you expected, you say it is more than you thought and ask them to check it against their records once, then accept the figure they confirm.

When the representative gives you the amount and hands you the way to send the funds, you send it yourself as a wire, with the sender name exactly 'Lorraine Whitcombe' and exactly the amount they gave you. When they tell you the money has been received, you thank them and end the call.
